EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows both an unconjugated carbonyl (1723 cm⁻¹) and an alkene (strong C=C at 1652 cm⁻¹) with clear =C–H stretches (3031, 3099 cm⁻¹) and abundant aliphatic C–H (2953, 2896 cm⁻¹), fitting an allyl ester. The very strong 1294 cm⁻¹ band is consistent with an ester C–O stretch. The trio of bands near 890/911/952 cm⁻¹ matches well with terminal vinyl out-of-plane modes (~910/990, shifted) together with characteristic epoxide ring vibrations (~890 and ~915 cm⁻¹), and the 1251 cm⁻¹ feature supports an epoxide ring breathing mode. Among candidates, only 1 combines an allyl ester and an epoxide, explaining the 890–950 cm⁻¹ cluster and the 1251 cm⁻¹ band. A nitro group (candidate 2) would typically show a strong ~1530–1560 cm⁻¹ band, which is absent.
